title: Practice: Threat Intelligence Platforms
prompt: Create a concise, reviewable artifact demonstrating Threat Intelligence Platforms. Use synthetic data or a controlled local training environment only. Include the relevant syllabus subtopics (Intelligence Repositories; Threat Feeds; Structured Threat Information), state assumptions, show what evidence would support your conclusion, identify one failure mode, and recommend a defensive next step. Do not test systems outside written authorization.

starter.use: Synthetic records or authorized local lab only

expected_output: A small, reviewable threat intelligence platforms artifact with scope, evidence, risk or limitation, recommended control, and a verification step.
acceptance_criteria: Use only a synthetic dataset, a disposable local lab, or an explicitly authorized system.
Include a clear scope/assumption statement and enough sanitized evidence for another learner to follow the reasoning.
Explain one limitation, edge case, or failure mode.
Recommend a proportionate defensive control and describe how to verify it safely.
hints: Start by naming the asset, behavior, scope, and expected result before drawing a conclusion.
Capture one normal example and one failure or boundary case; do not include real passwords, personal data, or production secrets.
Separate direct observations from hypotheses, then document a safe verification or rollback step.
grading_method: Server-side case-sensitive presence check for the listed report markers plus learner/coach review of correctness, context, evidence quality, and safety. This is a light submission gate, not an automated proof of security or a runner for submitted code.
retry_policy: Retries permitted after feedback. The server is responsible for recording completion once per exercise ID; this content file defines no XP override.
status_note: Draft instructional exercise; verify the rubric and all topic-specific details before publishing.
